card_roles.Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons: The mint, not the source: every -1/-1 counter you place buys a 1/1 deathtouch Snake, one per placement. Her combat trigger is a bonus on an unevasive 2/2 — do not attack into open blockers for one marginal counter.
card_roles.Yawgmoth, Thran Physician: The only mana-free sacrifice outlet here that also places a counter, which makes him the default tutor target. Always keep a second body on board: the ability carries one instance of "target", so an illegal target means no counter and no card.
card_roles.Mikaeus, the Unhallowed: Your only six-drop, and he places no counters himself. Cast him when Devoted Druid or Walking Ballista is already in play or in hand — alone he is an anthem and a small pile of undying triggers.
card_roles.Devoted Druid: Three green on the first pass and the one card that turns Mikaeus into a real loop. Without Mikaeus he is still a two-mana dork — play him on turn two and take the acceleration.
card_roles.Walking Ballista: Under Mikaeus with a free outlet it is the kill that needs no drain payoff at all. Alone, treat it as a scalable removal spell and spend counters on the creature actually attacking you.
card_roles.Blowfly Infestation: A repeatable counter source that feeds Hapatra every time a creature with a counter dies. Three of the deck's unsettled lines run through it — play it for the counters, not for a loop this manual has not verified.
card_roles.Nest of Scarabs: A second mint: your counter placements make 1/1 Insects as well as Snakes, so one sweeper pays twice. Deploy it before you cast Black Sun's Zenith, never after.
card_roles.Flourishing Defenses: The same exchange rate Nest of Scarabs gives you at three mana, for five, and it reads on any player's placement. Cast it when the cheap payoffs are already gone.
card_roles.Obelisk Spider: Your best converter: it drains each opponent on counter placement rather than on death, so a loop that places four counters per cycle pays four times. Fetch it first once a repeatable source is live.
card_roles.Zulaport Cutthroat: Table-wide drain on every creature you control dying, which is what turns a Snake wave into damage. Hold it as the converter for lines that run on a sacrifice outlet rather than on counters.
card_roles.Bastion of Remembrance: Zulaport on an enchantment that a creature wrath cannot touch, and it brings a body along. Lead with it against decks whose answers all point at creatures.
card_roles.Blood Artist: He drains one named player per death, so he is a value card and a wrath tax rather than a table clock. Take the life, and do not pivot on him alone.
card_roles.Skullclamp: Two cards for {1} on every 1/1 Snake — the best card-advantage engine in the deck by a distance. Clamp the token you were about to sacrifice anyway.
card_roles.Grim Haruspex: A card on every nontoken creature you control dying, which pays for Yawgmoth activations you were making regardless. He never sees your Snakes, so sequence him alongside real bodies.
card_roles.Morbid Opportunist: One card per turn from anybody's creature dying, which is free income in a four-player game. It triggers once each turn — do not hold your sacrifices back trying to squeeze more out of it.
card_roles.Deadly Dispute: A spare body becomes two cards and a Treasure at instant speed. Cash a Snake in response to targeted removal rather than in your own main phase.
card_roles.Village Rites: One black mana, two cards, instant speed. It is the cheapest way to make a wrath cost your opponents something.
card_roles.Night's Whisper: Two cards for two mana with no board requirement at all. Cast it on the turn your board is empty — that is the turn nothing else here draws.
card_roles.The One Ring: A turn of protection plus an escalating draw engine, paid for in life you already spend freely. Cast it when you need the turn off, not as a generic four-drop.
card_roles.Demonic Tutor: Two mana, any card, no strings. Point it at a repeatable -1/-1 source unless the table is one turn from killing you.
card_roles.Grim Tutor: Demonic Tutor for one more mana and three life. Count the life first — Yawgmoth, Bitterblossom and three painlands are all billing the same total.
card_roles.Diabolic Intent: Any card for two mana and a creature you were going to sacrifice anyway. Feed it a Snake and the cost rounds to nothing.
card_roles.Vampiric Tutor: One mana at instant speed, and it costs you your next draw. Cast it on the opponent's end step so the card arrives on time.
card_roles.Imperial Seal: Vampiric Tutor at sorcery speed. Fire it on a turn you had spare mana, not on the turn you need the card in hand.
card_roles.Worldly Tutor: A creature to the top of your library for one green at instant speed. Yawgmoth and Devoted Druid are the two names it should be finding.
card_roles.Survival of the Fittest: Repeatable creature tutoring for one green a shot, and the discard is close to free with Phyrexian Reclamation in the graveyard. Use it on every turn with a spare mana.
card_roles.Green Sun's Zenith: It puts the creature onto the battlefield instead of into your hand — Devoted Druid at X=2, Ivy Lane Denizen at X=4. That tempo is why it beats a card tutor on a tight turn.
card_roles.Ashnod's Altar: A free outlet and two colourless per body, which is a wrath dodge and a burst of mana in one card. Beside Mikaeus it buys one extra death — sequence it as a value activation.
card_roles.Phyrexian Altar: The coloured version at one mana per creature, and the colour is what makes it the better card here. Same rule beside Mikaeus: value, not a loop.
card_roles.Carrion Feeder: A one-drop free outlet that grows on every sacrifice. It adds +1/+1 counters, which fights your own plan — feed it Snakes and keep it away from creatures you want dead.
card_roles.Viscera Seer: One mana, free outlet, and a scry per body smooths every draw you take. It is the outlet to deploy on turn one.
card_roles.Blasting Station: A free outlet that untaps whenever a creature enters, so a Snake wave becomes a damage wave. Point the damage at whoever is closest to winning.
card_roles.Yahenni, Undying Partisan: A free outlet on a hasty body that goes indestructible on demand — your cleanest answer to a removal spell aimed at your own board. Sacrifice a Snake in response and keep everything.
card_roles.Fume Spitter: One mana that sacrifices itself to place a counter: a Snake, a dead X/1 and a death trigger for {B}. Save it to kill a mana dork rather than spending it on turn one.
card_roles.Serrated Arrows: Three counters over three turns from an artifact most creature decks simply cannot answer. Spend them one per turn for three separate Hapatra triggers.
card_roles.Contagion Clasp: It enters placing a counter and then proliferates every turn for {4}. Value the proliferate as removal you can repeat — how many Snake triggers a single mass placement yields is not settled here.
card_roles.Grim Affliction: A counter plus a proliferate at instant speed: a Snake, a shrink and a Crumbling Ashes target all in one card. Cast it on a blocker, not on your own turn.
card_roles.Crumbling Ashes: It destroys a creature carrying a -1/-1 counter every upkeep, and this deck always has one available. It is your only repeatable answer to a recurring threat — mark the target the turn before.
card_roles.Black Sun's Zenith: One card that wipes, mints fresh Snakes off the same placement and arms Necroskitter. Pick the X that kills their board and accept that your Snakes go with it — the tokens you get back enter clean.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: The reset button, and the one sweeper that pays you nothing: -X/-X places no counters, so Hapatra, Nest of Scarabs and Necroskitter all stay silent. Cast it to survive, never to build.
card_roles.Necroskitter: Every creature an opponent controls that dies with a -1/-1 counter on it comes back under your control. Put counters on their board before you sweep, not after.
card_roles.Host of the Hereafter: It enters with two +1/+1 counters and moves counters off your dying creatures onto a creature you choose. The loop it is famous for is unresolved here — play it as a four-mana body that recycles counters.
card_roles.Ivy Lane Denizen: It puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature whenever another green creature you control enters, and every Snake is green. Aim those counters away from your own fodder, since they cancel the -1/-1 counters you are trying to place.
card_roles.Scurry Oak: Evolve plus a Squirrel on every batch of +1/+1 counters, and its pairing with Ivy Lane Denizen is the highest-bracket line in the deck. That line is unresolved — use the Oak as a token maker until a scenario says more.
card_roles.Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER // Sephiroth,: A sacrifice outlet that draws on entry and on attack, plus a drain on every other creature dying. Four of those drains in one turn transforms him, and a Snake wave can supply them.
card_roles.Pitiless Plunderer: A Treasure for every other creature you control dying, which is how a long sacrifice chain funds itself. Deploy it before the chain starts, not halfway through.
card_roles.Bitterblossom: A body every upkeep for one life, from an enchantment a creature wrath cannot touch. It is keepable on its own — it rebuilds your board without any other card.
card_roles.Eternal Witness: Any card back from the graveyard, attached to a body you can sacrifice afterwards. Rebuy the sweeper or the tutor, not a mana rock.
card_roles.Phyrexian Reclamation: Two life and {1}{B} returns any creature from your graveyard, every turn, at instant speed. It is your recursion engine and it is what makes Survival of the Fittest's discard free.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Hexproof and indestructible for your whole board at two mana. Hold it for the wrath or the mass bounce, not for one targeted removal spell.
card_roles.Lightning Greaves: Haste for zero, which is what restores the mana half of the Druid loop. The shroud also stops Hapatra and Yawgmoth targeting whatever it protects — move it off before you activate.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for {1} to equip, and the hexproof leaves your own targeting alone. Put these on the creature you still need to target.
card_roles.Orcish Bowmasters: Flash, a ping and an Army token, and every extra card an opponent draws pings again. Hold it up on their turn rather than casting it on yours.
card_roles.Birds of Paradise: A turn-one dork producing either of your colours, which casts Hapatra on turn two. Later it is a body worth sacrificing like any other.
card_roles.Llanowar Elves: One green on turn one, and fodder afterwards. Deploy it immediately — there is no turn where holding it is better.
card_roles.Elvish Mystic: Identical to Llanowar Elves and just as welcome. Two dorks in an opener means a turn-two commander plus a spell.
card_roles.Dark Ritual: Three black from one, which is a turn-one Bitterblossom or a turn-two Yawgmoth off two lands. Spend it on a permanent, not on a tutor.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless on turn one that nothing in your curve is too coloured to use. Cast it first, every time.
card_roles.Mana Vault: Three colourless now against an untap step later. Fire it on the turn you are deploying the engine, not on turn one for its own sake.
card_roles.Grim Monolith: Three colourless with a {4} untap this deck can afford in the late game. It buys turns, not fixing — it adds no coloured source at all.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Two mana for a rock that taps for either of your colours. It is the one artifact here doing fixing work; the rest are colourless.
card_roles.Lotus Petal: One mana of any colour, once, for free. Crack it on the turn the commander or a tutor is exactly one short.
card_roles.Chrome Mox: Free acceleration that eats a coloured card out of your hand. Only fire it when the hand has a genuine spare — in a two-land keep it usually does not.
card_roles.Mox Diamond: Free, and it taps for either colour, at the price of a land from hand. Thirty-six lands means you can usually pay that — but never from a two-lander.
card_roles.Fixing lands: Twenty-two of your twenty-four land entries make both colours and none of them enters tapped, so colour is almost never why a turn stalls. Play the painlands — City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Tarnished Citadel — while your life total is still fresh.
card_roles.Utility lands: Eight lands do a second job: Grim Backwoods converts a body into a card, Lazotep Quarry is an outlet and a late reanimator, Abstergo Entertainment exiles every graveyard including yours, Talon Gates of Madara phases out a creature, and Svogthos, the Restless Tomb becomes a threat when your board is gone. Activate them on turns you were not casting anything.
card_roles.Basic lands: Seven Swamps and seven Forests, the only fourteen sources in the deck that answer just one question. Lead on a basic when the painlands can wait a turn.

combo_lines.001:
The clause that decides this is undying's intervening “if”: return it “if it had no +1/+1 counters on it” (CR 702.93a). Undying hands it back wearing exactly one; the off-switch is inside the ability.

The claim was that Hapatra supplies the reset. Annihilation is automatic (CR 704.5q); her placement is a combat-damage trigger (CR 113.3c) that cannot be interleaved between sacrifices. Holding: the claim fails as written. A token yields zero iterations, a nontoken one — disposing of Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Blasting Station and Yahenni, Undying Partisan.

Mikaeus with Devoted Druid is unbounded in deaths, counters, Snakes and drain — not in mana (CR 302.6). It assembles in 2.5% unassisted, 31.7% with a tutor, mean turn 5.69. Walking Ballista with Mikaeus is unbounded as a three-card assembly (CR 613.4c). Yawgmoth loops, bounded by the library his own draw empties (CR 104.3c).

The combo sheet claims nineteen two-card infinites in these colours. This record verifies one, downgrades a second, refutes six, and on the remaining eleven it is silent.

cover.identity: You are playing a converter, not a combo pile. Hapatra does not make -1/-1 counters at will — her first ability is a combat-damage trigger on an unevasive 2/2 — she monetises counters that *other* cards place, at a rate of one 1/1 deathtouch Snake per placement event. The 99 around her is built so that every counter becomes a body, every body becomes a card or a drain, and a narrow but genuine combo ceiling sits above a very strong grindy median.

how_it_wins:
The table counts the combo sheet in your colours and treats you like a fuse. Here is the truer read, and it is better news: Hapatra is a mint, not a source. Her combat trigger rides an unevasive 2/2 and is worth at most one extra counter per swing, so stop building turns around it. The half you actually play is the payout — every time you put -1/-1 counters on a creature she hands you a 1/1 deathtouch Snake.

So hunt sources, not payoffs. Eight sacrifice outlets in this deck cost no mana and exactly one of them, Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, also places a counter. You draw a tutor in 78.0% of games — point the first one at a repeatable source and never at a drain. Blowfly Infestation, Serrated Arrows, Contagion Clasp and Black Sun's Zenith are the same job on different bodies; cast whichever one this turn's mana can afford.

Most games you win by out-carding three people and then draining them, and that game assembles 67.2% of the time at mean turn 3.62. Pace for it. Clamp a Snake for two cards, cash a spare body to Deadly Dispute or Village Rites at instant speed, and let Grim Haruspex collect your creatures while Morbid Opportunist collects everyone else's. Every Snake you leave home blanks an attacker of any size, so the board that draws you cards is the board nobody wants to attack into.

The kill is one repeatable source plus one converter that hits all three seats, and you hold a converter in 51.9% of games. When the second half arrives, count the table's spent interaction and go — prefer Obelisk Spider, which drains on counter placement rather than on death and so pays four times per Druid cycle. Blood Artist names one player per death: take the value, do not call it a clock. One standing constraint on all of it — nothing in the 99 destroys an artifact, an enchantment or a land, so play around resolved permanents rather than planning to answer them.
mana_base:
Thirty-six lands across twenty-four entries, and zero of them enter tapped. Twenty-two make both colours; the other fourteen are basics, seven Swamps and seven Forests. That is a mana base with no tax on it — every land you draw works the turn it arrives.

Twenty-nine black sources and twenty-nine green from lands alone, against a target of twenty-two apiece. Seven over on both sides, which is why lands by themselves put each colour at 96.2% on curve. The 90% yardstick is usually the thing ramp exists to rescue; here it is cleared before a single rock is counted.

Now the disagreement an audit exists to find. Black carries 71.4% of the pip load — 40.0 pips over 34 cards, running as deep as triple black — while holding a 50% source share. Green carries 28.6%, 16.0 pips over 15 cards, on the same 50%. A twenty-one-point gap between what a colour asks and what it holds is normally an invoice, and it costs nothing here, because twenty-two of the lands answer either question.

Sixteen nonland producers finish the job: nine rocks, five dorks, two rituals. They lift on-curve to 98.8% black and 99.1% green and tilt the nonland source count green, ten to eight, because three of the five dorks make only green. Five of the rocks — Sol Ring, Mana Vault, Grim Monolith, Ashnod's Altar and Chrome Mox — score zero coloured sources under the unconditional-mana rule. They are buying turns, not colours.

None of it is free. City of Brass, Mana Confluence and Tarnished Citadel bill you in life; Forbidden Orchard hands an opponent a Spirit every time you tap it. Restricted mana: none — not one source here arrives with a spend-this-only clause. Zero taplands is an invoice paid on a life total, and the shape of the payoff is 2.464 mana on turn two, 6.15 by turn six, while the land-drop hit rate slides from 90.2% on turn three to 54.0% on turn six.
matchups:
They price you off your removal count. Fourteen interactive copies all aim at creatures: one class of five covered; artifact, enchantment, graveyard and land open. Sort every table by the type that beats you. One patch: Talon Gates of Madara phases a creature out, once — schedule it, never hold it.

Sweeper control thinks a wrath ends you. Assume it lands: tokens and cheap sources first, enabler in hand. You rebuild: Bitterblossom each upkeep for a life, Skullclamp two cards per dying 1/1, Grim Haruspex on nontokens, Blood Artist draining, Hapatra for two. Wrath with Black Sun's Zenith, not Toxic Deluge — counters on everything: a Snake, food for Nest of Scarabs, dying opponents' creatures for Necroskitter. Deluge only to clear the board.

Stax and tax is that hole plus no counterspell: the lock stays. Race under pieces two and three on what tax cannot touch: Yawgmoth (a life and a body), Bitterblossom (free upkeep), Hapatra (two mana). Politick the rest: admit no Winter Orb answer, buy the Krosan Grip for a turn of your counters elsewhere. A Gaea's Cradle or Cabal Coffers never dies: tax the player, removal at bodies, politics at mana.

Combo reads you as a slow token deck. Agree, then rank combo proximity above every board threat, every turn. Never aim at an artifact or enchantment kill; on a creature combo spend Grim Affliction, Fume Spitter, Serrated Arrows or Walking Ballista the turn it is live. Your clock — converter 3.34, Blowfly 4.10 at 16.3%, verified Mikaeus-Druid 5.69 at 2.5% — says win the deflection, not the race.

Aggro thinks 1/1s are free damage. That wall of deathtouch blanks any attacker: Snakes home, no swinging Hapatra into open blockers. Life is one pool — Yawgmoth, Phyrexian Reclamation, Bitterblossom, Toxic Deluge, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Tarnished Citadel — so defend the one real clock.

Creature midrange is your seat. Hold single-target removal until it points at you; on sight it profits two bystanders. Land Crumbling Ashes early, seeded by Fume Spitter or Grim Affliction: a countered creature dead each upkeep, a Snake per placement. Then win on cards: Skullclamp, Grim Haruspex, Morbid Opportunist, Deadly Dispute, Village Rites.

Graveyard hate at you is cheap: Rest in Peace costs Necroskitter, Phyrexian Reclamation and Eternal Witness, nothing more. Play full speed. Outward it is a schedule: Abstergo Entertainment exiles every graveyard for three and itself, so land it early against reanimator, spend before their payoff.
mulligan:
Everyone keeps the hand with Nest of Scarabs and Blood Artist in it. Do not be everyone. Those cards are exchange rates, and an exchange rate with nothing to exchange is a blank until the engine exists.

You can afford to be strict, because the deck is forgiving. You keep the first seven 79.9% of the time, average 0.243 mulligans, and put Hapatra on the table on turn two in 9,970 of 10,000 runs.

Keep on sight: two to four lands casting Hapatra on turn two, plus any of Yawgmoth, Devoted Druid, Blowfly Infestation or a tutor. Keep the two-lander with Birds of Paradise, Llanowar Elves, Elvish Mystic, Sol Ring, Lotus Petal or Dark Ritual attached — that hand casts the commander a turn early with a spell left over. Keep Skullclamp beside any token maker. Keep Bitterblossom alone; it makes a body every upkeep and rebuilds through a wrath by itself.

Ship the five-lander with no tutor and no dork. Four zero-drops, sixteen ones and nineteen twos means that hand is holding two cards it will never spend. Ship converters with no source — Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance are the classic trap keep. Ship hands built on Mikaeus alone; he is your only six-drop, he places no counters, and he needs a named partner.

Treat Scurry Oak, Ivy Lane Denizen and Host of the Hereafter as bodies rather than routes — the lines they are famous for are unsettled here. On the way to six, compress the test to two things: black mana on turn two, and one card that either places counters repeatedly or fetches one that does.
threat_assessment:
They see a 2/2 legend and two 1/1s and file you under snake deck. Keep that read until you spend it.

Hapatra lands turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs, so think about turn 3. A payoff joins her by turn 3.6 in 67.2% of games, so play four turns as the value deck.

Never sell nineteen infinites in a Rule 0 talk. Stack 001 verifies one, Mikaeus with Devoted Druid, and refutes six. Say bracket 4, eleven Game Changers, one verified line; the honesty buys the seat.

Play those six as written: with Mikaeus out, a sacrifice to Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer or Blasting Station buys one undying return and stops. Take the trigger, the card and the Snake; never announce a kill, tap out, or keep a hand for it.

Mikaeus and Druid assemble in 2.5% of games, 31.7% with a tutor, mean turn 5.69: hunt the tutor. Cast Blowfly Infestation, Scurry Oak and Host of the Hereafter as counter sources; the Hapatra-Blowfly pairing lands in 16.3% of games, 12.5% by turn 6: steer nothing at it.

Three cards flip you to archenemy, and Hapatra is not one. Yawgmoth is your only free repeatable source: land him with a second body down and a converting turn. Mikaeus costs six against 6.15 mean available on turn 6: cast him with Druid or Walking Ballista already down, or cast two other things. A drain converter beside a source is the pivot — Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance, Obelisk Spider, in hand in 51.9% of games, 41.5% by turn 6 — so hold one for that turn, not for removal to eat early. Deploy the Spider last: it drains on placement, not death, and reads as a kill.

Keep the cover: Bitterblossom, Snakes and cheap sources first, that half rebuilds through a wrath alone. Fast mana only on the turn it buys a threat.

These eleven spend it. Chrome Mox, Mox Diamond, Mana Vault, Grim Monolith, Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal, Worldly Tutor, Survival of the Fittest, Orcish Bowmasters, The One Ring. Fire tutors right after a louder seat acts. You draw one in 78.0% of games, 67.6% by turn 6: point it at a repeatable source, never a converter — four deep and it arrives alone. Cast The One Ring for cards on a turn you can pay the life and the attention.

Take the archenemy seat once, counted: open mana at every seat, every answer live, the attempt that leaves Bitterblossom, a converter and a board behind. Three seats overrate your combo record, so spend that discount on value turns — you out-draw this table far more often than you loop it.
upgrades:
One answered permanent class out of five: across all 88 entries, artifact, enchantment, graveyard and land go unanswered. Three of the ten aim there: Assassin's Trophy, Dawnhand Dissident, Boseiju, Who Endures. The first two take it to five of five, the cited target.

Boseiju's Channel answers an artifact, enchantment or nonbasic land from a land slot, free against 36 lands with zero taplands. But breadth counts interactive roles only, and a land is filed land:utility — the card works, the number doesn't move.

Ignition, a repeatable −1/−1 source costing no mana, is three cards. The payoff half is six deep at 67.2% assembled, mean turn 3.62. Four picks join it: Dawnhand Dissident, Sinister Gnarlbark, Evolution Sage, Persistent Constrictor.

Mikaeus is a component of one: 7.1% of an opening seven, his verified pairing with Devoted Druid 2.5% of games and 31.7% with a tutor. Redundancy, not mana. Gravecrawler and Reassembling Skeleton answer it, back after a wrath. No stack scenario has tested their altar lines, and stack 001 records seven of eight mana-free outlets placing no counter — nothing here is priced as a kill.

Drain converters read 51.9% assembled, two of four hitting every seat. Poison-Tip Archer and The Meathook Massacre widen that; Meathook modifies power and toughness instead of placing counters, feeding nothing on the Snake side.

Five cuts come out of ramp, 16 against a 10–12 band. Read it gently: four of the sixteen are engine pieces the taxonomy files as ramp, three of the five cuts are dorks, and Hapatra lands turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 games. Ten proposals, not a set; bracket floor 4 before and after.

The obsolescence index names fourteen cards here and produced no slot: it points at ramp and the sacrifice outlets, which the audit calls fine. Blowfly Infestation, the headline two-card kill at 16.3% assembled, runs on one copy; a scan of the 31 green-black cards holding “dies” and a −1/−1 counter found no chainer, and no stack scenario either.
